subject: Renewal: 8→16 GPU capacity request and billing/terms follow-up
messages:
From: Elisa Wong <elisa.wong@novalytics.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — need to double reserved pool for Q3

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for checking in on our renewal. We’re coming up on our annual renewal 7/15 and usage has continued to exceed projections — sustained token throughput for our realtime agents has pushed us close to saturation on the 8-GPU reserved pool. The engineering team ran a short load test last week and recommends moving to 16 GPUs to avoid throttling for peak windows.

Key asks from our end:
- Upgrade to a 16-GPU reserved pool for the next 12 months (starting 7/15).
- A throughput guarantee for 99th-percentile per-request latency under the new commit.
- Clarity on billing proration and invoice timing for the mid-month activation.

I attached the updated SOW and a short ops summary (Novalytics_SOW_v3.pdf). Can you share a rough cost delta and the operational playbook (activation window, lead time)? We’re also going to pull procurement in on our next reply.

Appreciate your help — Elisa

--
Elisa Wong
Director, Platform Engineering
Novalytics

Elisa — thanks for the note and the SOW. Appreciate the clarity on the timing. Quick answers up front: we can support a 7/15 activation for a 12-month 16-GPU commit, and we have options for a 99th%-ile latency target in the committed plan.

Action items I can take now:
- Share a preliminary cost delta and a short activation runbook (lead time, cutover windows, rollback plan).
- Schedule a 30-minute alignment call this week with our CS/ops and your engineering leads to validate target SLAs and peak hours.

Vivek — looping you in to confirm ops requirements and to flag any capacity pre-reservations.

I’ll attach our internal cost workbook and a draft amendment for your procurement to review.

Subject: Proposed amendment and pricing tiers for 16-GPU reserved pool (RW-4782)

Elisa — following Chloe’s message, attaching a draft amendment and two pricing options: Standard (month-to-month proration for mid-month activation) and Committed (12-month prepay discount with throughput guardrail). Highlights:
- Option A (Committed 12mo): 16 GPUs, predictable monthly commit, 12% discount vs month-to-month; includes two activation windows per contract year and a 99th%-ile latency SLA with credits tied to availability.
- Option B (Flex proration): 16 GPUs with proration on activation month, slightly higher unit rate, faster cancellation window.

We’ve included a DocuSign link for the order form in the amendment; procurement can redline the PDF as needed. Also: if Novalytics wants to stage activation (8→12→16) to spread activation risk, we can add a phased activation schedule and a small ramp fee.

Link to order form: https://docusign.com/RWD-4782-orderform
Attachment: RWD-4782-amendment-draft.pdf

Subject: Re: Proposed amendment and pricing tiers for 16-GPU reserved pool (RW-4782)

Thanks for the draft. A few procurement questions before we loop legal:
1) Proration math — if we activate 7/15, do we bill full month or pro-rate the activation month? Please provide the exact invoice example.
2) SLA credits — we need a clear credit table and the process for claiming. Does the SLA require monitoring hooks into our console or can we rely on Redwood’s telemetry?
3) Phased activation — we like the staged approach but need an explicit price for the ramp (8→12 for 30 days then 12→16).

Also attaching a short redline list for the amendment (we’ll send a marked PDF next). Can you confirm whether the 99th%-ile latency guarantee is measured at model endpoint latency or end-to-end request time?

Procurement will be available next Tue 6/8 for a quick call after legal reviews the redlines.

Regards,
Novalytics Procurement
From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: Novalytics Procurement <procurement@novalytics.com>, Elisa Wong <elisa.wong@novalytics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed amendment and pricing tiers for 16-GPU reserved pool (RW-4782)

Hi Elisa / Procurement team — following up with concrete answers and an agreed next step:

1) Proration: for a 7/15 activation we will pro-rate the activation month. Example invoice: full monthly commit = $48,000 for 16 GPUs; activation month (7/15) billed at 50% = $24,000, plus any overage usage at the monthly overage rate. We’ll include a sample invoice as a PDF in the next message.

2) SLA & credits: the 99th%-ile target we propose is measured at the model endpoint (per-request server-side latency). We can publish the measurement queries and provide a weekly latency report to Novalytics. Credit table summary: 0.5% credit for SLA miss up to 2%, 1.5% credit for 2–5% miss, >5% credit escalates to a billing review with potential larger credits per contract. Full table in the amendment. Monitoring hooks: we provide telemetry and raw traces; if you prefer we can add a telemetry export to your Splunk instance under a data-sharing agreement.

3) Phased activation pricing: 8→12 (30 days) = one-time ramp fee $6,000; 12→16 = no additional ramp fee if executed within the same 90-day window. We’ll model either approach in the final DOCS.

Next step: Marissa and I will update the amendment per your redlines and send it back to procurement + legal by EOD Thu 6/11. Can we confirm a signature target of 6/18 to allow ops to schedule the 7/15 activation?

Thanks — Chloe

Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
